name: OH-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Republican-leaning district (R+10) with incumbent David Joyce running for re-election
Overwhelming money gap: Joyce holds $3.1M on hand vs. roughly $34K for Maria Jukic
No outside spending opposing Joyce and no polling or expert ratings showing vulnerability
Prediction markets price the Democratic win chance near 2%
model.rationale: The district's ten-point Republican lean, Joyce's incumbency, and a cash advantage of more than 90-to-1 against a challenger with minimal resources point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets give Jukic only about a 2% chance. With no polls or expert ratings flagging risk, the forecast sits modestly below the incumbent's recent margins.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising, unexpected outside spending, or a scandal involving Joyce would be the main paths to a closer race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
OH-14 is a Republican-leaning Northeast Ohio district that David Joyce has held since 2013. He runs again with a large financial edge, having raised about $1.4 million and holding more than $3.1 million on hand. Democratic nominee Maria Jukic has raised roughly $63,000 with about $34,000 remaining, and no outside groups have reported spending for or against either candidate.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals: a ten-point Republican district, an entrenched incumbent, and a steep resource gap. Prediction markets put the Democratic win chance near 2%. Barring an unexpected development, Joyce is positioned for a comfortable re-election, with an expected margin in the mid-to-high teens.
